question: Abu’l Fazl was the court historian of which of the following rulers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Abu'l Fazl was a prominent court historian and one of the Navaratnas (Nine Gems) in Emperor Akbar's court.
 
• He authored the famous historical text **"Akbarnama"**, which chronicles the life and reign of Akbar in three volumes.
 
• The third volume of Akbarnama is known as **"Ain-i-Akbari"**, a detailed account of Akbar's administration, culture, and governance.
 
• Abu'l Fazl played a significant role in shaping Akbar's policies, including his religious policy of Sulh-i-Kul, which promoted tolerance and harmony among various religions.
 
• He was also a close advisor to Akbar and helped in the formulation of Din-i-Ilahi, Akbar's syncretic religious philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babar**

 
 
• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, reigned from 1526 to 1530.
 
• He was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan and authored **"Baburnama,"** his autobiography written in Chagatai Turkish.
 
• Babar is known for his victory in the Battle of Panipat (1526), which marked the beginning of Mughal rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**
 
 
• Alauddin Khilji was the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty and reigned from 1296 to 1316.
 
• He is known for his military conquests, administrative reforms, and market control measures.
 
• He successfully repelled the Mongol invasions and expanded his empire significantly.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
 
• Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, reigned from 1658 to 1707.
 
• He is known for his expansionist policies and strict adherence to Islamic principles.
 
• Aurangzeb imposed the **Jizya tax** on non-Muslims and is often criticized for his religious intolerance.
